extracted.intended_audience: researchers in natural language processing, AI/ML practitioners studying LLM evaluation and agent design
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating self-reflection interventions for large language model agents on problem-solving tasks (here: multiple-choice questions), measuring baseline performance, applying reflection-guided re-answering, and comparing reflection types with statistical testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance baseline using multiple-choice questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructed nine popular LLMs to answer a series of multiple-choice questions to provide a performance baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a clear pre-intervention baseline by having the selected LLMs attempt the target task (multiple-choice items) so that post-intervention improvement can be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reflection intervention procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each incorrectly answered question, we instructed eight types of self-reflecting LLM agents to reflect on their mistakes and provide themselves with guidance to improve problem-solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and implement distinct reflection protocols applied when an agent produces an incorrect answer; the reflection should analyze the mistake and generate specific guidance aimed at correcting reasoning or strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance-based re-answering
rubrics_metrics.description: Then, using this guidance, each self-reflecting agent attempted to re-answer the same questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the effect of reflection by having agents re-attempt the exact same items after consuming their generated guidance; use the re-answering outcome as the primary measure of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of reflection types
rubrics_metrics.description: We compared the various types of self-reflection to determine their individual contribution to performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple reflection variants (here: eight) and perform comparative analyses to attribute performance gains to specific reflection strategies or components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Our results indicate that LLM agents are able to significantly improve their problem-solving performance through self-reflection (p < 0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify improvements and report statistical significance (e.g., p-values) to support claims of effect; choose appropriate tests and thresholds and report them transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and selection of LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructed nine popular LLMs to answer ... to provide a performance baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select multiple, representative LLMs (here nine popular models) to improve generalizability of findings; document model choices and versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple reflection agent types (treatment variety)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each incorrectly answered question, we instructed eight types of self-reflecting LLM agents ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a repertoire of reflection agent types to probe which forms of reflection are most effective; explicitly describe each type so effects can be interpreted and replicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: code and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All code and data are available on GitHub at this https URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide publicly accessible code and datasets (with links) so that experiments can be reproduced, validated, and extended by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task selection: measurable problem-solving benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer a series of multiple-choice questions to provide a performance baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose task formats that yield unambiguous correctness (e.g., multiple-choice) to simplify pre/post comparisons and statistical analysis of improvement.
